subtitle: How a king of Malwa tried to bind the world with delight

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a lamplit royal library, scrolls rising like walls around a seated king
panels.action: Bhoja of Dhara sits cross-legged on a carved dais in his palace library, surrounded by stacked palm-leaf manuscripts, as a faint glow suggests scenes of lovers, forests and theatres reflected in a polished bronze mirror before him.

dialogue.text: In eleventh-century Dhara, King Bhoja wrote a vast Sanskrit mirror of delight—how could a warrior-king dare to tell the world what beauty itself should be?

i18n.hi: ग्यारहवीं सदी की धारा में, राजा भोज ने संस्कृत में आनंद का विशाल दर्पण रचा — एक रणबांकुरा राजा, जो दुनिया को बताने चला कि सुंदरता क्या है!

panels.shot: aerial wide over central India, drifting toward a fortified city on a plateau
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Malwa plateau shows the walled city of Dhara amid fields and rivers, with temples and palace towers rising under a hazy sun.

dialogue.text: Around 1010 CE, in the heart of Malwa, Dhara was more than a capital. It was a node in a Sanskrit world that stretched from the Narmada to the seas.

i18n.hi: लगभग १०१० ईस्वी में, मालवा के दिल धारा में सिर्फ राजधानी नहीं थी, नर्मदा से सागर तक फैली संस्कृत दुनिया की धड़कन थी।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a study, side-light catching dust motes over manuscripts
panels.action: Young Bhoja of Dhara leans over a low desk piled with palm-leaf manuscripts, a stylus in hand, while an armed guard waits respectfully at the doorway.

dialogue.text: Paramara Bhoja ruled with sword and seal, but he also bent over books. Traditions credit him with many texts, yet one work stands out as firmly his.

i18n.hi: परमार भोज तलवार भी चलाता, मुहर भी; और किताबों पर झुका रहता। परंपरा कई ग्रंथ उसके नाम करती है, पर एक किताब सचमुच उसकी लगती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Bhoja's hands and a single thick manuscript bundle being tied
panels.action: Bhoja's hands gently tighten cords around a bulky bundle of palm leaves inscribed with neat, dense Sanskrit, its edges darkened with use.

dialogue.text: The Shringara-Prakasha. One of the largest treatises on poetics and dramaturgy ever produced in Sanskrit, a king's attempt to systematise the very experience of art.

i18n.hi: ‘शृंगार-प्रकाश’ — रस और नाट्य पर संस्कृत का एक विराट ग्रंथ, जिसमें एक राजा खुद कला के अनुभव को नियमों में बाँधने निकल पड़ा।

panels.shot: medium shot, Bhoja addressed to unseen listeners, as if dictating
panels.action: Bhoja sits upright on a low throne in a simple hall, speaking calmly while a scribe at his feet etches his words onto palm leaves, a small oil lamp between them.

dialogue.speaker: bhoja_of_dhara
dialogue.text: Let us begin with rasa, for without it, no poetry breathes.

i18n.hi: चलो, रस से शुरू करें — रस नहीं तो कविता में जान ही कहाँ!

panels.shot: symbolic montage shot, Bhoja in foreground, faint layered images of classical Indian theatre behind
panels.action: Behind Bhoja's thoughtful profile appear soft, translucent scenes of a Sanskrit drama performance: actors in masks, musicians, a painted backdrop of a forest.

dialogue.text: Earlier theorists had named rasas, mapped moods, weighed words. Bhoja studied them all—and then chose a daring centre for his universe of art.

i18n.hi: पहले आचार्यों ने रस गिने, भाव नापे, शब्द तौले। भोज ने सब पढ़ा, और फिर कला के अपने ब्रह्मांड के लिए एक साहसी केंद्र चुना।

panels.shot: close-up on Bhoja's face, lit by lamp, eyes intent and reflective
panels.action: In the glow of a single lamp, Bhoja gazes at a polished metal mirror resting on his knee, his reflection mingling with faint painted figures of a loving couple on a nearby scroll.

dialogue.text: He placed shringara—love, desire, the play of attraction and separation—at the centre. An entire aesthetic system organised around delight in relationship.

i18n.hi: उसने शृंगार को, यानी प्रेम, कामना, मिलन-बिछोह के खेल को, बीच में बैठाया — रिश्तों के आनंद पर टिका पूरा सौंदर्यशास्त्र।

panels.shot: diagrammatic wide shot: Bhoja pointing to a manuscript as if teaching
panels.action: Bhoja gestures toward an open manuscript in which the artist suggests concentric circles and branching lists, hinting at systematic classification rather than literal diagrams.

dialogue.text: Page by page, he arranged causes and conditions of rasa. Determinants, expressions, transitory feelings—layered like steps that lead a listener from word to wonder.

i18n.hi: वह पन्ना-पन्ना रस के कारणों और हालात को सजाता गया। उपकरण, भाव, संचारी—सबको ऐसे जमाया कि सुनने वाला शब्द से चमत्कार तक पहुँच जाए।

panels.shot: medium shot in the same hall, a second lamp now illuminating more manuscripts
panels.action: More manuscript bundles lie open around Bhoja as he dictates, his free hand tracing invisible patterns in the air, as if weighing rival views.

dialogue.text: He argued with earlier authorities, adopted some, reworked others. The Shringara-Prakasha became a living map of Sanskrit poetics up to his time, through a Paramara lens.

i18n.hi: वह पुरानों से उलझा, कुछ मानें, कुछ बदले। ‘शृंगार-प्रकाश’ उसके समय तक की संस्कृत काव्य-परंपरा का जीवंत नक्शा बन गया, परमार नज़र से।

panels.shot: wide shot of a stylised map of the subcontinent, threads of script connecting cities
panels.action: A map-like view of the subcontinent shows Dhara, Kalyana, Kanchipuram and distant centres, linked by flowing bands of tiny Sanskrit letters arcing across hills and seas.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars call this the Sanskrit cosmopolis—a shared sphere of language tying courts, temples and scholars. Bhoja wrote for that world, not only for Malwa.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान इसे ‘संस्कृत कोसमोपोलिस’ कहते हैं—एक साझा भाषा-जगत जिसने दरबार, देवालय और विद्वानों को जोड़ा। भोज उसी संसार के लिए लिख रहा था, सिर्फ मालवा के लिए नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on a scribe’s hands carefully stacking copied leaves
panels.action: An anonymous scribe in another city carefully copies a section of the Shringara-Prakasha, stacking the finished leaves and wrapping them in cloth for travel.

dialogue.text: Copies travelled slowly along those routes, leaf by leaf. No eyewitness records of Bhoja's court survive, but his ideas walked where he could not.

i18n.hi: नक़लें उन रास्तों पर धीरे-धीरे चलीं, एक-एक पत्ती करके। भोज के दरबार की कोई आँखोंदेखी नहीं बची, पर उसके विचार वहाँ तक पहुँचे जहाँ वह नहीं जा सका।

panels.shot: wide shot of an 11th-century classroom in a temple or matha
panels.action: In a shaded verandah of a temple school, a teacher recites Sanskrit while students sit cross-legged, one holding an open palm-leaf text, listening intently.

dialogue.text: In halls like these, later generations weighed Bhoja’s schemes. Where does shringara begin? Can every poem be read through the light of one rasa?

i18n.hi: ऐसे ही सभागारों में बाद की पीढ़ियाँ भोज के सिद्धांत तोलती रहीं—शृंगार कहाँ से शुरू होता है? क्या हर कविता को एक ही रस की रोशनी में पढ़ा जा सकता है?

panels.shot: medium shot of a southern or western Indian poet in traveler's garb reading a manuscript
panels.action: A travelling poet in simple but dignified robes, seated at a roadside rest house, unfurls a manuscript labelled by design as coming from Dhara, his brow furrowed in concentration.

dialogue.text: For a poet on the move, Bhoja’s book was both guide and challenge, a royal voice saying: this is how delight can be understood, this is how words should work.

i18n.hi: चलते-फिरते कवि के लिए भोज की किताब राह भी थी, चुनौती भी—एक शाही आवाज़ कहती हुई: आनंद को यूँ समझो, शब्द यूँ चलाओ।

panels.shot: wide shot of a theatre performance with a thoughtful audience
panels.action: A night-time performance of a classical play unfolds under torchlight, with actors emoting on stage and a gathered audience, some visibly moved, others analytical and absorbed.

dialogue.text: On stage, love, loss and reunion played out as before. But now some spectators and playwrights thought with Bhoja’s categories, feeling their own feelings with new precision.

i18n.hi: मंच पर प्रेम, वियोग, मिलन पहले की तरह ही खेले जाते रहे, पर अब कुछ दर्शक और नाटककार भोज की श्रेणियों में सोचते, अपने ही भाव नए तेज से महसूस करते।

panels.shot: transition shot showing years passing: leaves drying, ink fading
panels.action: A time-lapse image shows palm leaves ageing: fresh green turning brown, ink lines fading slightly as the bundle is moved from shelf to shelf in different hands.

dialogue.text: Decades passed. Courts fell, new dynasties rose. The Shringara-Prakasha remained, a thick, demanding mirror asking each reader: what do you truly delight in?

i18n.hi: दशक बीते, दरबार ढहे, नए वंश उठे। ‘शृंगार-प्रकाश’ रहा—एक मोटा, कठिन दर्पण, जो हर पाठक से पूछता: सच में तुझे किसमें आनंद है?

panels.shot: medium shot of Bilhana in a later court, gesturing as he recites
panels.action: The Kashmiri poet Bilhana stands in a Deccan court, mid-recitation, one hand raised, while courtiers listen; a faint thought-image of a distant kingly figure hovers behind him.

dialogue.text: In the Vikramankadevacharita, Bilhana later recalled a king he never met. He lamented reaching Malwa too late—Bhoja was gone, his fame still alive in stories.

i18n.hi: ‘विक्रमांकदेवचरित’ में बिल्हण ने उस राजा को याद किया, जिसे उसने कभी देखा नहीं। वह दुखी हुआ कि मालवा देर से पहुँचा—भोज जा चुका था, उसकी कीर्ति बस कहानियों में जलती रही।

panels.shot: evocative medium shot: an imagined Bhoja seen from behind, overlooking his city at dusk
panels.action: Seen from behind in silhouette, Bhoja stands on a terrace above Dhara at dusk, the city’s rooftops below and a single manuscript cradled in his arm.

dialogue.text: We do not have eyewitness diaries of his court. What remains is the texture of his prose and argument, the way he folded a kingdom’s name into literary theory.

i18n.hi: हमारे पास उसके दरबार की दिनचर्याएँ नहीं, पर है उसकी गद्य-शैली और तर्क की बुनावट—जिसमें उसने अपने राज्य का नाम भी काव्य-शास्त्र में पिरो दिया।

panels.shot: close-up on the Shringara-Prakasha manuscript, Bhoja’s fingers resting lightly on it
panels.action: Bhoja’s aged hand rests on the open Shringara-Prakasha, the incised letters crisp, as if inviting the viewer to read; the background is lost in darkness.

dialogue.text: Here, delight is not an ornament but a principle. By centring shringara, Bhoja claimed that how we love, desire and imagine each other shapes the very measure of art.

i18n.hi: यहाँ आनंद सजावट नहीं, मूल नियम है। शृंगार को केंद्र में रखकर भोज कहता है: हम कैसे प्रेम, चाह और कल्पना करते हैं, वही कला की परख बदल देता है।

panels.shot: final wide shot mixing eras: a modern library faintly overlapping with an ancient one
panels.action: A modern scholar in a quiet university library studies a printed edition of the Shringara-Prakasha, while, ghostlike, an older scene of Bhoja’s manuscript hall overlaps behind him.

dialogue.text: From Dhara’s palm leaves to today’s printed pages, Bhoja’s mirror of delight asks the same question: what does a civilisation choose to feel, and how does it learn to feel it?

i18n.hi: धारा की तालपत्रों से लेकर आज की छपी किताबों तक, भोज का आनंद-दर्पण एक ही सवाल दोहराता है: एक सभ्यता क्या महसूस करना चुनती है, और वह सीखती कैसे है महसूस करना?

subtitle_i18n.en: How a king of Malwa tried to bind the world with delight
subtitle_i18n.hi: मालवा का एक राजा, जो दुनिया को आनंद की जंजीरों में बाँधना चाहता था
